newsitem.title: INDIA: Indias Deve Gowda pledges funds for Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Indias Deve Gowda pledges funds for Kashmir.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda pledged on Friday to increase federal funding to bolster the economy of the troubled Himalayan state of Jammu and Kashmir.

"Our primary responsibility is to restore the confidence of the people and the central government will provide full cooperation to the state government in reviving the economy of the state," he told a news conference in Jammu, the states winter capital.
The state government has submitted a proposal worth 25.16 billion rupees ($702.8 million) to Deve Gowda for strengthening its economy and he promised to take measures to implement it, officials said.
Deve Gowda said the state and the federal governments would jointly raise 1.5 billion rupees to complete a highway between Jammu and Srinagar, the states summer capital.

He said the federal government would provide a further 1.4 billion rupees to improve the 300-km (188-mile) national highway between Srinagar and Jammu and three billion to complete a 480-megawatt hydroelectric project in Uri.
The allocation of electricity to Kashmir would be increased to 816 megawatts to meet the states power shortage, he said.
Deve Gowda promised additional federal funds to Kashmir to restore infrastructure such as roads and bridges which were damaged by acts of militancy.
Over a dozen militant groups are fighting either for independence or Kashmirs merger with Pakistan. Jammu and Kashmir is mainly Hindu Indias only Moslem-majority state.
More than 20,000 people have been killed since 1990 when simmering discontent against Indian rule erupted into armed revolt.
